title: docs(adr 0017): prohibit storage-only surrogate keys project-wide
body:
## Owner decision: KEY-P01 — No storage-only surrogate keys

**Design-only Stacked PR on #57 / ADR 0016. No implementation or merge authorization.**

The owner adopts a repository-wide key design policy: **use domain-semantic natural/composite primary keys and corresponding composite foreign keys, instead of introducing arbitrary receiver-/database-local row surrogate IDs.** Apply across Git Core, durable Context, Operational and Search-facing authoritative interfaces.

### Binding semantics

- No gratuitous `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY`, auto-increment row IDs, separate UUID row IDs or duplicate one-column `id` in entities already identified by a semantic/composite key. Composite key width is an accepted cost; a shorter SQL join/ORM convenience is not enough to justify an extra authoritative ID.
- Nominal Git identity: directly use `(object_format, full_oid)` rather than a receiver-local `git_object_id`.
- Notes ref: repository UUIDv4 + exact full ref name plus genuinely needed origin/scope.
- Notes capture: directly use an origin-scoped composite domain identity, e.g. `(capture_origin_identity, capture_identity)`, as the **preferred as-yet-unselected B01-R03 key shape**; do **not** add `notes_ref_capture_row_id` purely to shorten FKs.
- Existing PR document natural composite key and meaningful Source↔repository relationships should remain direct, without duplicative record IDs.
- Search and SQLite may use internal physical implementation indices where unavoidable but may not promote index row numbers into durable domain identity or Exchange authority.

### Important existing-identity compatibility

This policy **does not revoke permanent `repository_uuidv4`**, which is already an owner-fixed domain identity. B01-R02 requires distinct genuine identical-root captures, while GCTX-M08 requires distinct physical copies of identical CAS bytes; neither can be uniquely represented by a content hash alone. Genuine durable domain **occurrence/instance** identity remains necessary, even if a generated UUID could in broad relational terminology be called a surrogate key. The ADR explicitly acknowledges this rather than disguising an arbitrary issued ID as a natural key.

A new identity token needs a documented, actually necessary domain distinction, unique issuer/scope, portability and trust semantics. It is **not** permission for a second local row ID. If the owner intends a literal ban on *all* newly generated occurrence identities, that would conflict with fixed repository/capture/physical-copy identity requirements and needs an explicit scoped decision before final DDL.

### B01-R03 next decision (not selected here)

The earlier receiver-local surrogate + portable-key option conflicts with KEY-P01. **Direct composite `(capture_origin_identity,capture_identity)` is recommended**, but issuer identity, allocation, repeated/partial Exchange and same-key conflict handling remain **open**. Neither the producer trust nor the replay grammar is selected by this PR.

### Scope and checks

- Add `docs/adr/0017-domain-keys-without-storage-surrogates.md` — owner policy, example keys, terminology/real-occurrence caveat, unchanged contracts, schema audit and future counterexamples.
- Update ADR 0016 B01-R03 choices (mark receiver-local surrogate incompatible; add direct-composite D as new candidate), ADR 0005 nominal identity, ADR 0012 physical-copy identity, ADR index, transition plan and root `AGENTS.md`.
- **Compare with #57 HEAD `896fbee08ed186897069558bc70d7f49a59325bb`: exactly one commit, seven Markdown paths, no code/SQL/DDL/schema-version/workflow changes.**
- HEAD: `c3cb94b367777b4a31d9dcf9644e253a69eef74a`; tree `3e3603905199d321aadcd0b5f0ea255957bfc43e`.
- GitHub compare verified the single direct-parent commit; ADR/readme/AGENTS/transition and predecessor cross-links read back. No runtime, SQL, PR merge, CI, release acceptance or independent coding review is claimed; documented examples are future requirements.

### Previously accepted decisions

Preserve ADRs 0003–0016 in their actually applicable scope, particularly permanent repository UUIDv4, nominal full Git object identity, B01-R01 ref discovery, B01-R02 immutable per-genuine-capture identity, ADR 0014 no ordinary file archive but retained notes, append-only Core/no-GC, Context independent durability, GCTX-M05–M09 retained byte/CAS integrity and CAS-41, exact five-column/latest-observation Coverage, Source known-positive, Unix epoch microseconds, NO_INDEPENDENT_PUBLICATION and ADR 0001 testing/release distinctions. GCTX-M10 and notes B02/B03 remain unresolved. Proposed sibling governance PR #52/ADR 0011 remains **unaccepted**.

## Owner-accepted B01-R02 — Option B: immutable capture-scoped notes observations

**Design-only stacked PR. Base: #56 / ADR 0015, which depends on #55 / ADR 0014 and the unmerged GCTX-M01–M09 design stack. No implementation or merge is authorized.**

The owner selected **B: one portable immutable capture identity per genuine notes-ref observation**, rather than the ref/root natural key or target/note relation. A repeated delivery of the same capture is idempotent, while independent observations of the same ref/root remain distinct.

### Binding architecture

- Explicitly separate **common Git nominal OID identity** `(object_format, full_oid)`, **notes-ref identity** (permanent repository UUID + exact full ref/source scope), **capture-scoped notes-ref observation identity**, **observation-scoped note mapping/member groups**, and optional permitted note-body bytes/verification.
- Example: K1 partial mapping of ref review at root A; K2 complete (if B03-supported) independently observed at the same root A; K3 later ref root B; K4 returns to root A. All four are immutable distinct actual observations. Re-delivery of **K2 itself** must not produce a fictional fifth capture.
- Capture identity is **portable across Exchange/repeat forwarding** in its referential semantics. However, its allocator/issuer namespace, origin-scoped idempotency key, receiver-local ID mapping, conflicting replay and partial-member extension rules remain the explicit next owner choice **B01-R03**; neither a raw OID nor capture timestamp is implicitly chosen as a capture key.
- Each capture retains available exact ref name, repository, source/capture evidence, observed root OID/type when actually known, and typed observed note-target/note-blob/path members. No forced root commit, fabricated body, missing-to-empty promotion, arbitrary union of groups, or current-ref winner by timestamp/arrival/UUID order.
- A replay claiming the same accepted capture with contradictory repository/ref/root/source facts cannot overwrite prior Git Core truth or be silently promoted by sender assertion. Exact collision/replay admission policy remains B01-R03.
- Capture facts are **Core-owned and Context-independent**. Provider assessments remain Context, transient jobs/retries Operational, Search derivative. Do not create a generic scan-attempt ledger, Publication seal, or Core mutable `current_notes_ref` pointer.
- B01-R01 notes ref discovery remains all observable `refs/notes/*` (including nested suffixes) plus explicitly nominated other refs. This **does not authorize ordinary file-blob archival**. Retain note content solely with actual typed role proof; never infer current CAS health from an observed ref/root.

### Prior design invariants

Fully preserve ADR 0014 (Git history/tree/tag/notes catalog, no ordinary file bodies), ADR 0015 (notes-ref discovery), GCTX-M01–M09 (nominal identity, claims/groups, canonical verification boundaries, retained byte/CAS integrity and immutable physical repair/selection), ADR 0003 strict append-only Core, CAS-41, permanent repository UUIDv4, known-positive Source, five-column latest-observation Coverage, Unix epoch microseconds `_us`, NO_INDEPENDENT_PUBLICATION, Context durability, and Core-only metadata import/query.

title: docs(adr 0015): accept B01 automatic Git notes ref discovery
body:
## Owner accepted B01 Option B: Git notes namespace discovery

**Design-only Stacked PR.** Base **#55 / ADR 0014** (GCTX-S01, history/structure/notes catalog without ordinary file archival), which is stacked on #54 → #53 → #51 → #50 → #49 → #48 → #47 → #46 → #45 → #44. All are unmerged. Sibling proposed governance #52 (ADR 0011) remains **unaccepted** and is not adopted by this PR.

### Binding owner selection / B01-R01

- **Automatically discover all observable `refs/notes/*` ref names** for the explicitly selected repository/source observation; this includes `refs/notes/commits`, arbitrary sibling names and nested suffixes (not merely a one-level shell glob).
- Allow **additional explicitly nominated notes ref names**, including outside `refs/notes/*`, retaining exact name/source provenance; a caller-provided role or prefix alone does **not** authorize persisting arbitrary file blob bytes.
- Discovery is scoped to the **actually observable inventory**; an unfetched/unadvertised remote notes ref is not proven absent. A failed, incomplete, not-attempted or empty-but-unverified enumeration must not be laundered into a complete-empty notes catalog or remote-wide completeness claim.
- Distinguish ref enumeration, ref-root observations (notes commit **or direct tree**; root kind may be unknown), typed notes mapping and allowed **note body** admission. A discovered ref is not a verified notes mapping, not a complete list, not proof all note blobs exist, and not an automatic fetch/body-storage permit.
- Default Git notes display settings are **not** exclusive ref-discovery selectors. Keep each namespace, observed root and provenance distinct; do not fabricate a globally current notes-ref winner or union unrelated capture groups.
- Automatic and explicit selection of the **same full ref name within one observation** does not itself create two distinct namespace identities. No conclusion about the durable capture/observation ID is made.
- Metadata-only Git Core with no original bytes or Context remains valid; tag/note references to ordinary blobs still never permit storing target file contents.

### Prior contracts retained

ADR 0014's product-purpose boundary (no ordinary file blob archive; retain commit/tree/tag representations and evidence-backed notes content); GCTX-M01–M09 (nominal OIDs, per-field claims, observation-scoped typed groups, qualified/canonical reads, Core ownership of Git verification, bounded byte admission, operation-scoped CAS checks, immutable alternate physical copies and deterministic non-authoritative eligible-set selection); strict Git Core append-only, no independent Publication, CAS-41, Coverage five-column/latest-observation semantics, Source known-positive, permanent repository UUIDv4, Unix epoch microseconds, Context durability and Core-only metadata operation all remain binding. GCTX-M10 quarantine disposition/count is still open.

### Next question, explicitly **not accepted**

**B01-R02:** durable identity for a notes-ref **observation/capture** when the same ref/root is seen twice, changes and returns, or is reported by distinct sources. Alternatives: (A) ref/root natural key; (B) immutable capture-scoped ID with distinct genuine observations and idempotent replay (recommended); (C) target/note relation as the primary identity. Resource limits and note-body admission proof B02, and scoped completeness B03 remain open.

### Changed files and checks

title: docs(adr 0014): retain Git history and notes, remove ordinary file archival
body:
## Accepted scope revision: GCTX-S01 / ADR 0014

**Design-only stacked PR on #54. No implementation, data purge or merge authorized.**

The owner requests excluding original-content archival from the product while continuing to store commit/tree/tag/note. This records the explicit product-purpose boundary: **ordinary repository-file blob bodies are not archived, but Git history/structure/tag representations and actual notes content are retained.** This is not merely an archive mode disabled by default.

### Retained and excluded domains

- Retain nominal full OIDs, source-attributed attributes/ordered relations, repository identities and ref observations without requiring any original bytes or Context (GCTX-M01–M03).
- Retain commit/tree/annotated-tag metadata and exact representations when actually acquired and validated, without making raw bytes a prerequisite to metadata-only import. Preserve messages, names, ordering and supplied signatures; do not manufacture raw serialization from normalized API data.
- Retain **Git notes content and scoped associations**. Notes are native Git **blobs**, not a fifth object type. A blanket `type != blob` filter is incorrect. Notes scope includes namespace/ref, observed root, target OID, note OID/path where known and capture evidence.
- Exclude ordinary file-body archival and its optional/general upload, hydration, whole-file recovery, source full-text storage and arbitrary raw export paths, including hidden duplicates in Search, Context, caches and pending Exchange.
- A tag or note **targeting** an ordinary blob does not authorize archiving the target's bytes. A shared file/note blob OID keeps one nominal identity with separate roles. Notes may be binary and may share bytes with a file; this is a product-purpose boundary, not a guarantee that no stored annotation can equal arbitrary file content.
- Preserve Context PR/Issue/review text; it is not repository file-original archival.

### Scoped prior-decision changes

ADR 0014 explicitly narrows new raw-body admission from arbitrary Git objects to retained metadata/notes. M04–M09, exact OID/CAS checking and CAS-41 still protect those retained bodies. **Do not delete their integrity machinery merely because ordinary file archival is removed.** M10 physical quarantine disposition/count remains unresolved; this PR does not adopt any of its alternatives or automatically zero quarantine counts.

No Core UPDATE/DELETE/REPLACE/GC is allowed. The new scope is not permission to delete prior catalogs or relabel actual retained-byte loss as never acquired. A future fresh-catalog extraction must be separately authorized, scope-reported and preserve source catalogs/backups absent explicit deletion permission.

Catalog backup/restore remains supported, including mutually consistent Core+Context backups where applicable. Full Git mirror restoration, source-file checkout and complete raw repository bundles are not product promises. A verified tree/commit does not verify referenced file bodies or prove full byte closure.

### Documentation changes

Exactly **four Markdown paths**, one commit above #54:

- Add `docs/adr/0014-history-and-notes-catalog-without-file-archive.md`: accepted scope, notes exception, precise supersession, retained guarantees, open design boundaries and primary Git references.
- Redesign `docs/architecture/git-core-context-transition-plan.md`: logical notes model, grouped source-schema impact, acquisition/retention gates, scope-aware integrity/search/Exchange/backup and dependent implementation stages.
- Update `docs/adr/README.md`: current applicability of all retained decisions and the explicit ADR 0014 override.
- Reconcile `AGENTS.md`: new scope first, condense repeated historical status summaries while retaining applicable architecture, domain, authorization, validation and reusable-skills rules. Do not let older handoffs reintroduce generic file archival.

The group inventory is **not** a completed 70-table/call-site audit. Exact physical DDL, notes-ref discovery defaults, resource limits and association/verification grammar remain to be fixed. Note bodies are not assumed small or UTF-8, and no silent truncation policy is introduced.

### Base, checks and limitations

- Base #54: `0301fcc8aeef427e2b9e2a3197a4ed993dcdf657`, re-read before branch creation; still open/unmerged.
- Head: `4a45a137ee22ec1c87fb616bc94aef5587918737`.
- Tree: `7ad097422b78235d20deaebc797e43845adb7075`.
- GitHub compare confirms one commit and only the four Markdown paths above. The new ADR was read back from this exact commit.
- Primary Git docs checked: git-notes, Git object model and git-cat-file.
- A disposable **Git 2.47.3** fixture confirmed note content is blob, binary notes round-trip exactly, notes refs may point directly to trees, and one blob may simultaneously serve as a file and note. No `git-repo-db` runtime or DDL was executed.
- Container download of the full source was blocked by DNS resolution. Repository reads/writes used connected GitHub tools. No full checkout build, MkDocs/site build, product runtime/CAS/Exchange tests, hosted-CI success or independent review is claimed.

### Parallel-stack coordination

PR #52 / ADR 0011 remains a separate **proposed** governance change off #51; it is neither adopted nor merged here. ADR 0014 was checked against current PR/index allocation. Earlier design PRs remain unmerged and unchanged on their own branches; this successor provides the scoped product override. Resolve shared index/AGENTS edits only during explicitly authorized integration.

No Python, SQL/DDL, workflow, dependencies, schema labels, live catalog, release, deployment, publication allowlist or authenticated source acquisition changes. **Do not merge or implement until explicitly authorized.**

title: docs(adr 0013): fix GCTX-M09 deterministic CAS physical-instance selection
body:
## Accepted owner decision: GCTX-M09 — Option A

**Design-only Stacked PR.** Directly based on #53 / ADR 0012 (GCTX-M08), which is stacked on #51 → #50 → #49 → #48 → #47 → #46 → #45 → #44. All remain **unmerged**. No implementation or merge permission is granted.

The owner selected **A: derive the eligible physical-instance set from immutable evidence and select candidates deterministically**, rather than maintaining mutable active pointers, choosing by time/source, or requiring manual selection for every duplicate.

### Binding policy

- Candidate eligibility is a **read-only Git Core projection** from one coherent snapshot, based on independently identified original/repair physical copies, local byte-admission/CAS associations and the absence of effective known instance-specific disqualifying evidence.
- Eligible means **allowed to attempt current validation**, not “proven physically healthy now”. An old success scan, absent fault report or nominal Git OID alone never establishes current health.
- If several candidates I2 and I3 qualify for a logical payload H, order by a **stable immutable catalog-local physical instance identity** (or equivalent fixed non-authoritative tie-break). No canonical Git object winner, preferred parser, source credibility or “latest acquisition wins” is inferred. Exchange receivers may have different instance IDs and try order without semantic conflict.
- Verified byte-returning operations must check the **actual emitted bytes** against CAS SHA-256 and the corresponding Git OID/type/size, with GCTX-M07’s coherent read/output scope; known damaged/quarantined I1 remains excluded.
- On detecting newly corrupt I2 bytes, **do not publish them as verified**; persist the necessary immutable physical-instance-specific diagnosis and re-evaluate eligible candidates under a coherent snapshot before a safe retry of I3. If required durable fault recording fails, do not suppress the observed fault and announce a clean success.
- Metadata-only and historical canonical queries remain usable without any original bytes or Context, distinguishing reported/unverified, conflict and historical admission from currently healthy bytes.
- A healthy sibling I3 can restore **logical payload byte availability** without healing, erasing or silently removing I1/I2 from physical integrity evidence.

### CAS-41 and still-open predicate

CAS-41 remains binding: archived **active physical quarantine count** is compared to the copied and verified database’s count **before restore-time diagnosis**. It counts distinct qualifying **physical instances** under an exact policy to be selected in GCTX-M10, not historical event rows or unavailable logical payloads. Merely admitting I2 cannot automatically clear I1’s known fault or lower its active quarantine count.

**Next GCTX-M10**: whether damaged, retained physical instances remain actively quarantined permanently, may be formally retired from active outstanding quarantine only by narrow immutable disposition evidence (candidate recommendation), or may be retired by an independently supported automatic terminal-evidence rule. Irrespective of option, the physical damage and the bytes remain retained and ineligible for export; the exact count predicate must be fixed before implementing revised backup manifests.

### Previously accepted invariants unchanged

- GCTX-M01: metadata-only Git Core without bytes/Context or hidden fetch.
- M02: common full typed OID identity, separate from logical CAS and physical instance identity.
- M03/M04: source-attributed scalar and relation-group evidence; canonical verified values with visible conflicts; no merging incompatible reports.
- M05/M06: Git intrinsic verification and bounded immutable local admission evidence in Core; Provider assessment in Context; Jobs in Operational.
- M07: operation-scoped checks of the **actual delivered** original bytes; scanned-as-of is not healthy forever.
- M08: physically distinct immutable I1/I2 instances, instance-scoped diagnosis and recovery facts, no in-place repair.
- ADR 0003: **no Git Core UPDATE/DELETE/REPLACE or GC**, no fifth authoritative store, no generic Publication.
- Preserve permanent repository UUIDv4, Source known-positive, exact five-column/latest-observation Coverage semantics, Unix epoch microseconds, CAS-41, sender-trust boundaries and ADR 0001 validation rules.

### Repository-state coordination

Proposed ADR governance [PR #52](https://github.com/TakashiSasaki/git-repo-db/pull/52) is a **sibling** of #53 based on #51, and reserves ADR 0011. Its policy is **not adopted** by this PR. GCTX-M08 is ADR 0012, and GCTX-M09 is newly allocated ADR 0013; the two parallel PRs change the ADR index/AGENTS.md and will require an explicitly authorized integration review before any merge. Do not rewrite or retarget #52.

### Changed documents and verification scope

- Add `docs/adr/0013-deterministic-cas-instance-eligibility.md` containing the accepted decision, worked three-instance example, formal scope separation, M01–M08 reconciliation and **15 future acceptance counterexamples**.
- Update ADR 0012, ADR 0010/0009 references, ADR index, Git Core/Context transition plan, and root `AGENTS.md`.
- Compared with #53 HEAD `df0689b3a06bb1a46233737f444eb64527ec5db5`: **exactly one commit, seven Markdown paths only**; no Python, SQL/DDL, CLI, schema version, GitHub workflows or runtime changes.
- Head `0301fcc8aeef427e2b9e2a3197a4ed993dcdf657`, tree `d08aea3f977415837ef366236ff9fef721866356`. Source files/ADR link targets, decision index and inherited stack were inspected; GitHub compare establishes intended ancestry and changed paths.
- This is *design validation*, not executed CAS corruption/recovery/transaction, Exchange, release test, hosted CI acceptance or independent review. Future counterexamples are specification, not test receipts.

**No implementation, migration, merge, authenticated source acquisition, retained-catalog mutation, deployment or release authorized.**
